skill.name: micro-saas-launcher
skill.description: Plan and launch a focused micro-SaaS product through validation, MVP scoping, pricing, distribution, onboarding, and growth guidance.
skill.summary: Turn a focused SaaS idea into a validated launch plan with practical pricing, distribution, and retention guidance.

content.value_statement: Founders often waste time building broad products before validating demand or distribution. This skill creates a focused path from idea validation to launch and growth.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates product ideas against demand, willingness to pay, feasibility, and distribution access.
Scopes a two-week MVP around one core feature and a solo-founder technology stack.
Suggests simple pricing structures based on customer value and market type.
Builds pre-launch, launch-day, and post-launch action plans across common channels.
Diagnoses acquisition, conversion, onboarding, pricing, and churn problems.
Defines practical SaaS metrics, validation checks, and growth priorities.
limitations: Does not verify market demand without real customer interviews, sales, or experiment results.
Does not build, deploy, or operate the product by itself.
Pricing benchmarks are general guidance and require testing in the target market.
Legal, payment, authentication, and analytics recommendations require specialist review and implementation.

use_cases.title: Validate a New SaaS Idea
use_cases.description: Create a validation plan using interviews, competitor evidence, pre-sales, and a measurable landing-page test.

use_cases.title: Scope a Fast MVP
use_cases.description: Reduce a broad product concept to one core feature, a practical stack, and a two-week delivery sequence.

use_cases.title: Improve Early Revenue
use_cases.description: Review pricing, acquisition, onboarding, and churn signals to prioritize experiments that support sustainable recurring revenue.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this micro-SaaS idea: [idea]. The target customer is [customer]. Identify assumptions, red flags, and three validation tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before investing significant development time.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Two-Week MVP
prompt_templates.prompt: Scope a two-week MVP for [product]. Define one core feature, excluded features, recommended stack, daily milestones, and launch readiness criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after initial demand evidence exists.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pricing and Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Create pricing and launch plans for [product] serving [market]. Use these alternatives and costs: [details]. Include channels, assets, and success metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when preparing to acquire the first paying customers.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Growth Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this micro-SaaS using the following metrics and feedback: [data]. Diagnose acquisition, activation, conversion, and churn constraints. Prioritize five experiments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an operating product with customer and revenue data.

output_examples.input: Validate a scheduling tool for independent tutors.
output: Interview five tutors who currently coordinate lessons manually.
Test willingness to pay with a focused pre-sale offer.
Measure landing-page conversion from a tutor community.

output_examples.input: Scope an MVP for automated client status reports.
output_examples.output: The MVP centers on importing one data source and producing one shareable report. Custom branding, teams, and advanced integrations remain outside the first release.

output_examples.input: Review a product with strong signups but weak paid conversion.
output_examples.output: First compare acquisition source, onboarding completion, feature usage, and upgrade intent. Then test clearer value delivery, a simpler paid tier, and targeted customer interviews.

best_practices: Provide a specific customer, problem, current alternative, and available evidence.
Validate willingness to pay before expanding the MVP scope.
Track one measurable outcome for each launch or growth experiment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat broad interest or waitlist signups as proof of payment demand.
Do not add multiple features before the core value is delivered reliably.
Do not depend on launch-day attention without a repeatable distribution channel.

faq.question: What stage is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It supports idea validation, MVP planning, launch preparation, and early recurring-revenue growth.

faq.question: Does it write the application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides product, launch, pricing, and growth guidance that can inform separate implementation work.

faq.question: Can it guarantee product-market fit?
faq.answer: No. Product-market fit requires real customer behavior, payments, retention, and repeated market testing.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the customer segment, problem, alternatives, pricing assumptions, acquisition channels, constraints, and any available metrics.

faq.question: Does it support business-to-business and consumer products?
faq.answer: Yes, but its guidance favors focused products with clear buyers, reachable audiences, and sustainable payment demand.

faq.question: Are its legal and financial recommendations authoritative?
faq.answer: No. Use qualified legal, tax, privacy, and financial professionals for decisions specific to your business and jurisdiction.
